newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast gasoline down sharply with NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast gasoline down sharply with NYMEX.

text.p: U.S. West Coast gasoline prices dropped Wednesday, in reaction to weaker energy futures prices and the disappearance of supportive fundamentals.
Wholesale unleaded gasoline prices in California dropped 7.8 percent to 76 cents a gallon, down six cents from from late Tuesday and 10 cent fall from a week ago, traders said.
The decline was led by a 2.06-cent fall on NYMEX gasoline futures for May delivery, which closed at 60.61 cents.
"The Merc's been really weak, there are no buyers and lots of sellers," one broker said, referring NYMEX gasoline futures.
Traders also attributed the drop to weaker fundamentals, with Tosco and refinery workers averting a strike by agreeing to a new five year labor agreement last weekend.
Conventional grade was talked lower, falling nine cents to 68.50 cents a gallon.
Distillates held firm amid rumors of a possible supply disruption from ARCO's Carson, refinery south of Los Angeles.
ARCO denied a rumor which claimed the facilities diesel-making unit was malfunctioning, causing ARCO to raise its prices at truck terminals.
Low sulphur diesel stayed 67.50/68.50 cents a gallon, even with Tuesday, with CARB grade diesel fell 1.50 cents a gallon.
